messages:
amanda: Heads-up — deploybot paused v2.9.3-rc3 canary. SBOM policy flagged a transitive dep 'libsec' with CVE-2025-1234 (medium). Change window today 17:00-20:00 UTC. Need quick decision: pin vs rollback vs scoped rollout. @ben_security @matt_sre :rotating_light:

deploybot: Automated: release v2.9.3 canary PAUSED by policy `sbom-vuln` (severity=medium, count=1). Affected job: canary-01/us-west-2. Actions: review required to resume or rollback.

ben_security: Triage update: CVE-2025-1234 affects libsec <2.4 and is exploitable in a specific API used only by the analytics optional plugin. Our default runtime does NOT call that API. Impact: low for default installs, higher for customers with analytics enabled. Recommendation: allow a scoped canary (beta customers / internal) while we prepare a patch/backport to remove the vulnerable transitive dep.

kira_product: What's the customer-facing surface here? Any telemetry showing customers hit the vulnerable code path? Who owns release notes / comms if we keep canary? :eyes:

matt_sre: Telemetry so far: no increase in 5xx or latency, p99 steady. Canary hosts healthy. Suggest: hold global rollout, allow limited canary only (us-west-2, internal/beta), add runtime flag to disable analytics plugin: `--disable-analytics-plugin`. Watch for 45m, rollback on policy/traces.

ashley_product: If we go canary-only we need a clear RN note and account ops blurb for customers who opted into analytics. I'll draft a short customer notif and RN entry.

deploybot: Tip: resume command available: `deploy resume v2.9.3 --targets=canary --regions=us-west-2`

ben_security: Proposed plan:
1) Accept canary-only risk (security approves for scoped rollout).
2) Backport fix (PR #4821) to remove/replace vulnerable transitive dep and add package resolution.
3) Add runtime guard flag to disable plugin for affected customers.
4) Block global rollout until PR merged + CI + verification.

Decision: security +1 for canary with controls. :thumbsup:

kira_product: +1 from product. I'll own release notes and coordinate account ops. Creating a follow-up ticket to track comms.

ashley_product: Created ticket PROD-1123 for customer notif and RN draft. tagging @legal for wording for regulated customers.

legal: Quick ack — ok to proceed with canary-only, please include phrase 'temporary canary-only acceptance' and notify customers with regulated deployments directly.

matt_sre: Resuming scoped canary now for us-west-2 (10% traffic, internal/beta only). Rollout policy: 10% ramp, 45m steady-state watch. Auto-rollback triggers: error rate > 0.5% or policy breach. Monitor: https://monitoring.redwood/canaries/123

amanda: OK — action items summarized: ben open PR and link here, matt resume canary and watch, ashley push RN & customer notif, kira coordinate account ops, legal signoff included. We'll reconvene at 18:15 UTC to decide on wider rollout.

ben_security: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4821 — includes lockfile resolution and unit test coverage. CI ETA ~20m.

kira_product: Noted. Flagging for on-call to watch customer channels.

matt_sre: Canary resumed at 17:20 UTC. Monitor link above.

deploybot: Automated: canary resumed v2.9.3 in us-west-2. Auto-rollback configured.

amanda: Thanks everyone. Leaving thread open until PR merges and we clear global rollout. Created follow-up REL-3581 to track patch, legal note, and rollout decision. :white_check_mark:
